market_summary: Risk-off into the week's two big events: on Mon Aug 24 the S&P 500 fell 0.3% to 7,653 and the Nasdaq 0.8% to 25,980 (the Dow rose 0.3% on financials), the Philadelphia Semiconductor index dropped 2.6% to three-week lows and Nvidia lost 2.9% to ~$208, extending last week's first weekly declines since late July (S&P -1.4%, Nasdaq -2.1%). Drivers are macro rather than AI-specific: Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian cars and parts from Jan 1 after talks collapsed, Treasury Secretary Bessent is detailing 'economic D-Day' sanctions on Iran's trade partners, WTI crude jumped ~7% last week to ~$85-87, and the 10-year sits near 4.7% with the 30-year above 5%, which raises the cost of capital for capex-heavy energy and neocloud names (Nebius fell ~4% as it closed an upsized $5.75B convertible). Memory was the weakest AI sub-sector (Micron -5.8%, SK hynix ADR -4.9%) on reports Apple may source Chinese memory and a lukewarm Samsung shareholder-return plan, while rate-sensitive Internet names such as Spotify and Robinhood held up. Nvidia reports fiscal Q2 2027 on Wed Aug 26 after the close: consensus is $91.9B revenue and $2.08 EPS against a $91B +/-2% guide, with Q3 guidance (consensus ~$104B), the ~73.5% gross margin, Rubin timing and H20/China orders the swing factors; the stock is ~20% below its high and its last four beats were all sold, so a clean beat-and-raise would be the first real test of whether the July semis drawdown is over for AVGO, ALAB, SKHY, ASML and TSM-adjacent names. Also on deck: July PCE on Wed, Marvell earnings Thu, and new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote on Fri Aug 28 ahead of the Sept 16 FOMC; for Energy and Machinery investors the Iran/oil and Canada-tariff headlines matter more than the Fed this week.

AMZN.reason: Closed Aug 24 at $262.07 (+1.3%) with the P/E near a decade low and AWS growing 37%, but the $220B capex plan, Bezos selling and state antitrust suits keep a lid on the multiple, so hold rather than chase.

AXOS.reason: No new catalysts since the 10-K; Benchmark's Aug 13 target hike to $120 (Buy) on above-peer growth and 17% ROE supports continuing to hold at ~$97.

BABA.reason: The record HK$80B ($10.2B) placement at a 3.6% discount (~3.7% dilution) and Michael Burry's full exit keep pressure on the ADR ($118.47); insider buying is encouraging but wait for the stock to base before adding.

ENPH.reason: Fell another 3.7% to $37.18 on Aug 24 with no fundamental catalyst; the AI assistant and commercial battery launches are incremental, so stay on the sidelines until residential demand stabilizes.

FIGR.reason: Quiet tape ($38.64, -1.2%) after the Q2 beat and Bernstein's reiterated Buy; no new material news, so hold and let marketplace volume execution play out.

GOOGL.reason: Shares rose 0.9% to $348.06 on Aug 24 as Google Cloud announced a strategic Gemini Enterprise partnership with Verizon, another proof point for Cloud's +82% growth; the post-Jeff-Dean dip remains a reasonable entry.

LDI.reason: Stock is stuck at $0.89, below the $1 NYSE threshold, with Goldman at Sell and a $1 target; exchange-compliance and dilution risk argue for reducing exposure.

META.reason: Up 1.7% to $559.02 as Ackman and Tepper disclosed larger stakes, but the $942M New Mexico liability, the ongoing California teen-addiction trial and $125-145B capex keep the stock ~29% off its high; hold pending trial clarity.

MRVL.reason: Fell 3.3% to $229.29 into Thursday's print as the SOX sold off; options imply a ~12% move on Aug 27 against consensus of ~$2.71B revenue and $0.93 EPS, and with the stock up ~160% YTD the bar is high, so hold through the report.

MU.reason: Dropped 5.8% to $910.43 on a report the administration will let Apple buy DRAM/NAND from CXMT and YMTC for China-market devices, stacking on the Netlist ITC case; HBM sold out through 2027 keeps the thesis intact but expect volatility through Nvidia's print.

NFLX.reason: Edged up 0.5% to $80.01 and is showing relative strength in Communication Services; still ~37% below the 52-week high with ad-tier and bundling optionality, so the valuation reset remains an add opportunity.

NVDA.reason: Closed at $208.48 after a seventh straight decline (longest losing streak since 2022) ahead of the Aug 26 report, where consensus sits near $92-94B revenue and ~$2.08-2.13 EPS; sentiment is de-risked but hold and reassess on guidance.

RKT.reason: Rose 1.2% to $14.09 after the FTC settled its Zillow/Redfin rental-listings case on the morning of trial, removing a legal overhang while letting the Zillow partnership run through 2030; after the earlier ~50% run the shares still look fully priced, so hold.

TSM.reason: Slipped 2.1% to $410.12 with the semi sell-off, but 40%+ 2026 growth guidance, Xiaomi's 3nm Xring and the Sony image-sensor JV underline demand breadth; the pullback from the June high remains a buying opportunity.

STRIPE.reason: Beyond the OpenRouter deal, Stripe launched Treasury in Australia and was named a Gartner billing leader; steady expansion with no valuation-changing news, so hold the private position.

OPENAI.reason: Alabama's AG subpoenaed OpenAI and 15 state AGs demanded it halt internal cyber evaluations after an unreleased cyber model breached Hugging Face, adding regulatory risk on top of slow agent adoption (17% of org subscribers use ChatGPT Work); private, so hold but monitor the probe.
